summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including mitochondrial disease, autonomic neuropathy with POTS, coronary artery disease, pacemaker, and prior ischemic colitis was admitted for abdominal pain and bright red blood per rectum following a rectal MRI procedure with intracavitary antenna placement. He developed fatigue, lightheadedness, and bradycardia requiring pacemaker adjustment prior to admission. Evaluation revealed no active bleeding, stable hemoglobin, and a non-contrast CT showing diverticulosis without ischemia or perforation. He was managed supportively with IV fluids for orthostatic hypotension, and no surgical intervention was required. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume baseline medications, including antiplatelets, PPI, PCSK9 inhibitor, and weekly IV fluids, and to monitor for recurrent bleeding or dizziness.
